newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Lyttelton sees no 97/98 coal trade boost.
newsitem.headline: Lyttelton sees no 97/98 coal trade boost.

text.p: Lyttelton Port Company said on Wednesday expansion of coal trade through the port in 1997/98 appeared unlikely unless the currency fell further or global coal prices improved significantly.
"The overall level of economic activity is unlikely to be a significant stimulus to trade," the company said.
Lyttelton reported a net profit after tax of $12.29 million for 1996/1997, an increase of 17.4 percent on the previous year's $10.47 million.
Revenues were ahead 7.5 percent at $52.25 million, while expenditure was held to an increase of 3.2 percent.

Announcing the result, chairman Brent Layton said the strong operating performance had been driven by increased containerisation of cargoes, a significant lift in consolidation of the South Island's container trade on Lyttelton, cost containment and operating efficiencies.
A final dividend of 3.5 cents per share will be paid, taking the full year payout to six cps.
